# libtmux for Ruby Create tmux sessions, split windows, send input, and capture pane output from Ruby. Read server state into a [snapshot][snapshot], then query it with [`where`][selection-where], [`select`][selection-select], and the rest of `Enumerable`. [![compatibility](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml) [![libtmux](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux?label=libtmux)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/LICENSE)
Install the core gem: ```console $ gem install libtmux ``` It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer on `PATH`; a [server handle][server] refuses an older daemon before running a command. An [MCP server][mcp-application], an Async adapter, and a workspace loader ship beside the core under [Packages](#packages). ## Quick start Create a session, add a window, split it, and print each window with its panes: ```ruby require "libtmux" snapshot = LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session( name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"] ) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.snapshot end snapshot.windows.each do |window| puts "#{window.name}: #{window.panes.map(&:id).join(', ')}" end ``` Save it as `quickstart.rb` and run it: ```console $ ruby quickstart.rb ``` It prints: ```text main: %0 logs: %1, %2 ``` [`Server.start`][server-start] gives the program a tmux server of its own, on its own socket with an empty configuration, and closes it when the block exits. It never touches a tmux you already use. Pane commands take argument arrays. ## Drive a pane ### [`Pane#split`][pane-split]: split a pane, type into it, resize it [`send_text`][pane-send_text] types literal text, [`send_keys`][pane-send_keys] sends key names such as `Enter`, and [`capture`][pane-capture] reads the screen. [`Pane#resize`][pane-resize] and [`Window#resize`][window-resize] set sizes in cells: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| created = server.new_session( name: "work", command: ["/bin/sh"], receipt: true ) pane = created.pane side = pane.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"]) pane.send_text("echo ready") pane.send_keys("Enter") line = nil 50.times do line = pane.capture.stdout.lines(chomp: true).find do |text| text == "ready" end break if line sleep 0.1 end puts "captured: #{line}" created.window.resize(width: 100, height: 30) side.resize(width: 20) puts "side pane: #{side.snapshot.width} columns" end ``` It prints `captured: ready` and `side pane: 20 columns`. [`Entity#kill`][entity-kill] removes a pane, window or session, and [`Server#kill`][server-kill] stops a daemon. More: [pane input and capture](docs/reference/behavior.md#pane-input-and-capture). ## Find things in a snapshot ### [`Server#snapshot`][server-snapshot]: one read, many queries [`where`][selection-where] takes criteria as data and [`select`][selection-select] takes a Ruby block. Both filter the snapshot locally and make no tmux calls: ```ruby require "libtmux" snapshot = LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session( name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"] ) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.snapshot end panes = snapshot.panes active_ids = panes.where(active: true).map(&:id) wide_panes = panes.select { |pane| pane.width >= 40 } panes_by_window = panes.group_by { |pane| pane.window.name } logs = snapshot.windows.one(name: "logs") missing = snapshot.windows.one_or_nil(name: "missing") puts "active: #{active_ids.join(', ')}" puts "wide: #{wide_panes.map(&:id).join(', ')}" puts "logs panes: #{logs.panes.length}" puts "missing: #{missing.inspect}" ``` It prints: ```text active: %0, %1 wide: %0, %1 logs panes: 2 missing: nil ``` - [`one`][selection-one] raises [`NoMatchError`][nomatcherror] or [`MultipleMatchesError`][multiplematcheserror] unless exactly one record matches. [`one_or_nil`][selection-one_or_nil] returns `nil` for none. - A selection keeps the membership it captured. Call [`server.snapshot`][server-snapshot] again to see later changes. More: the [field catalog][doc-fields] and the [list and filter recipe](examples/list_filter.rb). ### [`Server#explain_panes`][server-explain_panes]: what runs in tmux, what runs in Ruby [`explain_panes`][server-explain_panes] returns the plan for a pane query and sends nothing to tmux. [`search_panes`][server-search_panes] runs it. Today tmux returns the whole server and Ruby applies every criterion: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) criteria = {active: true} plan = server.explain_panes(where: criteria) puts "tmux reads: #{plan.fetch(:capture)}" puts "tmux filters: #{plan.fetch(:pushed) || 'nothing'}" puts "Ruby filters: #{plan.fetch(:residual).fetch('where').keys.join(', ')}" puts "matching panes: #{server.search_panes(where: criteria).length}" end ``` It prints: ```text tmux reads: full_graph tmux filters: nothing Ruby filters: active matching panes: 1 ``` More: [execution modes][doc-modes]. ### [`Window#snapshot`][window-snapshot]: read one object again A record is what tmux said when it was read. Ruby has no `refresh` that updates a record in place, as Python libtmux's `.refresh()` does: read the object again. [`Window#snapshot`][window-snapshot] returns a new record and leaves the one you hold as it was. [`Session#snapshot`][session-snapshot] and [`Pane#snapshot`][pane-snapshot] do the same: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session( name: "work", window_name: "editor", command: ["/bin/cat"] ) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) held = window.snapshot window.rename("build") puts held.name puts window.snapshot.name end ``` It prints: ```text editor build ``` Each call reads the whole server, as [`server.snapshot`][server-snapshot] does, and returns the one record you asked for. ## Run several commands in order ### [`Server#run_group`][server-run_group]: several commands through one client A group sends several tmux commands, in order, through one client. The [`GroupResult`][groupresult] holds one aggregate status, and each step reports `unknown`: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) group = server.run_group([ ["set-option", "-g", "@before", "kept"], ["select-pane", "-t", "%4294967294"], ["set-option", "-g", "@after", "never run"] ]) puts "success: #{group.success?}" puts "steps: #{group.steps.map { |step| step.fetch(:outcome) }.join(', ')}" puts "@before: #{server.options(scope: :session).get('@before').as(:string)}" end ``` It prints: ```text success: false steps: unknown, unknown, unknown @before: kept ``` The first command keeps its effect when the second fails, and the third never runs. More: the [group recipe](docs/recipes.md#failure-inside-a-group). ## Watch tmux change ### [`Server#open_control`][server-open_control]: events as they happen A [`ControlConnection`][controlconnection] runs a command with [`exchange`][controlconnection-exchange] and streams what tmux reports through [`subscribe`][controlconnection-subscribe]. The subscription's [`next`][controlsubscription-next] waits for the next [`ControlEvent`][controlevent]. It needs tmux 3.7 or newer: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) server.open_control(session: session.ref) do |control| reply = control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 5) puts "reply: #{reply.blocks.last.body.strip}" events = control.subscribe(max_events: 64, max_bytes: 65_536) window.rename("renamed") event = nil until event&.raw&.start_with?("%window-renamed") event = events.next(timeout: 5) end puts "event: #{event.raw.strip}" end end ``` It prints: ```text reply: ready event: %window-renamed @0 renamed ``` More: the [control overflow recipe](docs/recipes.md#control-overflow). ## Use the tmux server you already run ### [`Server.new`][server-new]: borrow a daemon [`Server.open`][server-open] and [`Server.new`][server-new] bind an endpoint that already exists, such as `Server.open(socket_path: ...)`. Closing the binding leaves the daemon running. The outer [`Server.start`][server-start] block here only supplies a daemon to borrow: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |owner| owner.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server = LibTmux::Server.new(endpoint: owner.endpoint) begin puts "connected sessions: #{server.list_sessions.length}" ensure server.close end puts "sessions after client close: #{owner.list_sessions.length}" end ``` It prints: ```text connected sessions: 1 sessions after client close: 1 ``` More: [ownership and errors][doc-ownership]. ## Packages Start with `libtmux`. Add the companion for your caller: | Gem | Require | Use it for | | --- | --- | --- | | [libtmux](gems/libtmux/README.md) | `libtmux` | Blocking scripts, snapshots, and control connections | | [libtmux-async](gems/libtmux-async/README.md) | `libtmux/async` | Concurrent commands and bounded streams in Async tasks [![libtmux-async](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-async?label=libtmux-async)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-async) | | [libtmux-mcp](gems/libtmux-mcp/README.md) | `libtmux/mcp` | An MCP server with explicit endpoints and tool policy [![libtmux-mcp](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-mcp?label=libtmux-mcp)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) | | [libtmux-workspace](gems/libtmux-workspace/README.md) | `libtmux/workspace` | YAML/JSON workspace plans and a CLI to apply them [![libtmux-workspace](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-workspace?label=libtmux-workspace)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-workspace) | Requiring a gem starts no tmux process, scheduler, or protocol server. [Execution modes][doc-modes] compares blocking calls, Async tasks, and control subscriptions. ### [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux): the core Blocking [server][server], [session][session], [window][window] and [pane][pane] handles, immutable [snapshots][snapshot], and [control connections][controlconnection]. Require `libtmux`. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) ```console $ gem install libtmux ``` More tasks, in the [core README](gems/libtmux/README.md): - [Type into a pane and read it back](gems/libtmux/README.md#type-into-a-pane-and-read-it-back) - [Wait, time out, and cancel](gems/libtmux/README.md#wait-time-out-and-cancel) - [Read and set options and hooks](gems/libtmux/README.md#read-and-set-options-and-hooks) - [Link a window into several sessions](gems/libtmux/README.md#link-a-window-into-several-sessions) ### [libtmux-async](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-async): concurrent commands Concurrent commands and bounded control streams inside an Async task that your application owns. Require `libtmux/async`, then open a scope with [`LibTmux::Async.open`][async-open]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/libtmux-async/) · [Guide](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/async/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-async) ```console $ gem install libtmux-async ``` Capture every pane concurrently with [`Scope#map`][async-scope-map]: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| refs = scope.server.list_panes.map(&:ref) screens = scope.map(refs, concurrency: 2) do |ref| scope.server.pane(ref).capture end puts "captured panes: #{screens.length}" puts "all succeeded: #{screens.all?(&:success?)}" end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text captured panes: 2 all succeeded: true ``` ### [libtmux-mcp](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-mcp): a tmux server for MCP clients An MCP server over stdio for one tmux server, with an explicit tool policy. Installs `libtmux-mcp`; require `libtmux/mcp` to embed it through [`LibTmux::MCP::Application`][mcp-application]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/reference/) · [Tools](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) ```console $ gem install libtmux-mcp ``` Add the server to Claude Code. `--start-session work` starts a tmux server on the socket `agent` when none answers there, with a session named `work`, and stops it when the server exits. Until you enable more tools, the server serves [`tmux_capabilities`][tool-tmux_capabilities] and [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: ```console $ claude mcp add tmux -- libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --start-session work \ --endpoint dev ``` More: the [MCP README](gems/libtmux-mcp/README.md) covers other clients, every tool and authored shell commands. ### [libtmux-workspace](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-workspace): YAML workspaces YAML or JSON workspaces, validated, planned offline and applied to an open server. Installs `libtmux-workspace`; require `libtmux/workspace` to use it from Ruby through [`LibTmux::Workspace`][workspace]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/reference/) · [Command reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/cli/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-workspace) ```console $ gem install libtmux-workspace ``` Save this workspace as `workspace.yaml`: ```yaml session_name: work environment: PROJECT_MODE: development windows: - window_name: editor window_index: 1 layout: tiled panes: - shell_command: printf 'editor ready\n' - {} ``` Check it without contacting tmux: ```console $ libtmux-workspace validate workspace.yaml ``` ```text Workspace configuration is valid. ``` More: the [workspace README](gems/libtmux-workspace/README.md) loads it into a running server and lists every option. ## What it leaves out - **Live objects.** A [snapshot][snapshot] record is what tmux said when you read it, and a selection keeps the membership it captured. Read again to see a change. - **A terminal emulator.** [`Pane#capture`][pane-capture] returns what tmux's `capture-pane` prints for the pane. - **A server it starts unasked.** [`Server.new`][server-new] and [`Server.open`][server-open] bind a running server; only [`Server.start`][server-start] starts one. With no socket named, [`Endpoint.new`][endpoint-new] picks the socket tmux would, so a program run inside tmux reaches that tmux. See [Endpoints][doc-endpoints]. - **Whole-program typing.** RBS declarations ship with each gem. See the [public methods][doc-api]. - **Throughput claims.** The [benchmarks][doc-benchmark] list their workloads and limits. ## Support and status - **Unstable API.** Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and any release may change or remove exported identifiers. Pin an exact version. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), which links each gem's own. - **Ruby 3.3 or newer** and **tmux 3.3a or newer.** A [server handle][server] refuses an older daemon before it runs a command. Release candidates are not supported. See [Release candidates][rc-policy]. - **Control connections need tmux 3.7 or newer.** On an older daemon `open_control` raises `UnsupportedFeatureError`, and `Server#supports_control?` returns false. The [optional-feature table][doc-optional-features] and [`capabilities.json`][capabilities-json] list the other releases. - **Linux, including WSL, and macOS.** CI runs on Linux; macOS is best effort. See the [compatibility workflow][compat] and the [CI matrix](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#running-ci-against-any-tmux). # Execution modes

| Mode | Wait and ownership | Result evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core command | Calling thread blocks; server binding owns each client and its pipes | `CommandResult` has binary stdout/stderr and final client status |
| Captured query | Snapshot acquisition performs explicit I/O; `Selection` filtering is local | Stable captured membership with acquisition interval and coverage |
| Command group | One client submits an ordered, nontransactional group | Aggregate final status; individual steps remain `unknown` |
| Core control | One owned reader thread drains the connection; each subscriber has limits | Guarded blocks between boundaries; hooks can share the interval |
| Async | Caller supplies an Async parent task; pipe I/O yields on its scheduler | Same command evidence, with bounded request admission and cancellation |
| MCP | Caller supplies transport streams, Async scope and tool policy | Versioned protocol envelopes and structured tool responses |
| Workspace | Parsing and planning are inert; apply performs ordered commands | Created-reference ledger, observed effects and explicit uncertainty |

## Servers

- `Server.open(socket_path: ...)` borrows a daemon through a pinned binding.
  With no socket named, it borrows the daemon tmux would pick. See
  [Endpoints](reference/behavior.md#endpoints).
- `Server.start` creates an owned daemon on a unique socket and closes it with
  the block.

## Results

- `CommandResult#success?` means the client exited successfully. Sending input
  does not show that a shell finished.
- A `GuardedReply` has no `success?`: `%end` ends a guard, and WAIT commands,
  aliases and hooks can change what finishes when. Its `boundary_window`
  attribution is weaker than per-command ownership.

## Control connections

- Concurrent calls pipeline complete requests on one connection. The writer can
  submit a later request while an earlier reply waits, and the reader assigns
  boundaries in the same order. Sequential calls still wait for each reply.
- Admission limits count every pending request and every completed request
  whose reply nobody has consumed.
- Cancelling after any request bytes are written closes the connection. Other
  written requests report `possibly_sent` delivery, and requests with no
  written bytes report `not_sent`. Nothing uncertain is replayed.
- A reliable subscription raises `SubscriptionOverflow` when it cannot keep the
  stream. A tail subscription emits a gap with the lost sequence and byte
  counts. Neither blocks the command reader behind a slow consumer.
- Limits apply to connection-owned buffers. Callers own the replies they keep.

## Captured queries

- A query evaluates the whole criteria tree before selecting rows, including
  inactive OR branches.
- Explain methods perform no I/O. Current source plans capture explicitly and
  evaluate locally. A required pushdown with no exact compiler fails rather
  than change semantics.

More: the [recipes](recipes.md) cover WAIT release, cancellation, overflow and
group failure.

# Ownership and errors

- A reference holds a binding identity, a kind and a tmux-assigned ID. Window
  links also keep session and index context, so one window at several indexes
  is still one window.
- Names are query values, not stable command targets.
- A borrowed binding keeps its private socket route. Replacing the public
  socket does not make it follow a new server.
- Closing a binding retires its clients and pipes and leaves a borrowed daemon
  running. A server from `Server.start` also owns its daemon and temporary
  directory.
- Handles, Async tasks and subscriptions stay with the process and scheduler
  that made them.

| Failure or empty value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Empty `Selection` / `one_or_nil` returns `nil` | A valid complete local selection has no matching record |
| `NoMatchError` / `MultipleMatchesError` | `one` cannot establish exactly one match |
| `InvalidFilterError` / `FieldDecodeError` | Criteria or wire values do not satisfy the declared schema |
| `IncompleteSnapshotError` | Required coverage is unavailable; do not infer absence |
| `TargetNotFoundError` | The guarded target no longer matches its identity/context |
| `Cancelled` / `DeadlineExceeded` | The requested wait ended; delivery evidence determines possible effects |
| `SubscriptionOverflow` / gap event | A bounded stream cannot establish uninterrupted delivery |
| `Workspace::ApplyError` | Inspect its immutable result ledger before deciding whether to compensate |

## Delivery

Operation errors report a phase and delivery evidence: `not_sent`,
`possibly_sent` or `observed`.

- An observed nonzero exit still needs its command result.
- A cancelled mutating request can already have effects.
- A timed-out WAIT lock request can still take its queued lock after a later
  unlock. Retiring the client does not roll back tmux's command queue.
- Cleanup diagnostics accompany failures. A cleanup failure is not a
  successful close.

## Cancellation

- Cancelling an owned command client sends TERM, then KILL if its exit is not
  observed, and reaps the child within the remaining cleanup deadline. There is
  no grace period for a TERM handler. Borrowed panes and daemons are never
  terminated.
- Pass `LibTmux::Cancellation.new` as `cancel:` to blocking requests. Calling
  `cancel` from another thread wakes every user of the token, and `cancelled?`
  stays true. Later requests with the token refuse before dispatch.
- A token can cancel several requests. It owns a pipe and starts no thread. Keep
  it open until every request using it has returned, join those callers, then
  call `close`. Closing does not join them.
- `cancel` and `close` are idempotent, and their return values are unspecified.
  `reader` belongs to the token: do not consume its bytes or close it. After a
  fork, a child can close its inherited descriptors but cannot query or cancel
  the parent's token.
- The [plain-Ruby example](../examples/cancel.rb) shows wakeup, delivery
  evidence and client reaping. Async tasks use `Task#cancel`, as the
  [Async example](../examples/async_cancel.rb) shows.

## Workspace compensation

- Compensation is explicit. It removes only a session the apply positively
  created, whose current windows and panes all belong to its creation ledger,
  checked in the same tmux command turn.
- A borrowed window or pane moved into that session prevents it.
- Arbitrary shell effects cannot be rolled back, and an unacknowledged creation
  is never guessed by name.

## Redaction

Parsing errors and ordinary inspection redact payloads. Explicit results,
captures, plans and canonical exports hold the data you asked for, including
commands and normalized paths. You control how it is stored and shown.

See [execution modes](modes.md) and the
[workspace README](../gems/libtmux-workspace/README.md).

## Blocking request cancellation

[Complete plain-Ruby cancellation program](../examples/cancel.rb). A tmux event
shows dispatch before another thread cancels the blocked client. The program
joins the caller, checks that the client was reaped, and closes the token.

<!-- example: cancel/main -->
```ruby
cancellation = LibTmux::Cancellation.new
waiting = nil
begin
  waiting = Thread.new do
    server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"],
      timeout: 0.5, cancel: cancellation)
  rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error
    error
  end
  server.wait_for("ready", timeout: 0.5)
  cancellation.cancel
  failure = waiting.value
  Example.check(failure.is_a?(LibTmux::Cancelled), "cancellation lost")
  Example.check(failure.delivery == :possibly_sent, "dispatched wait claimed no effects")
  Example.raises(Errno::ECHILD) { Process.waitpid(failure.pid, Process::WNOHANG) }
  Example.check(server.diagnostics.fetch(:admitted_requests).zero?, "client remains admitted")
ensure
  begin
    cancellation.cancel
    waiting&.join
  ensure
    cancellation.close
  end
end
```
<!-- /example -->

## Async capture and cancellation

[Complete Async program](../examples/async_cancel.rb). A second task captures
while another tmux client waits; cancellation retires that client's process.

<!-- example: async_cancel/main -->

```ruby
  LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope|
    waiting = parent.async do
      scope.server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"], timeout: 0.5)
    rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error

    end

    end

    waiting.cancel
    failure = waiting.wait
    Example.check(failure.is_a?(LibTmux::Cancelled), "cancellation lost")
    Example.check(failure.delivery == :possibly_sent, "cancelled dispatch claimed no effects")
    Example.raises(Errno::ECHILD) { Process.waitpid(failure.pid, Process::WNOHANG) }
    Example.check(scope.server.diagnostics.fetch(:admitted_requests).zero?, "cancelled client remains admitted")
  end
end.wait
```

## Control overflow

[Complete control program](../examples/control_overflow.rb). It needs tmux 3.7
or newer and demonstrates the refusal on older daemons. A slow reliable
subscriber fails explicitly; a tail subscriber reports a gap and replies
continue to drain.

<!-- example: control_overflow/main -->
```ruby

  control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 0.5)
  reliable = control.subscribe(max_events: 1, max_bytes: 1024)
  tail = control.subscribe(mode: :tail, max_events: 1, max_bytes: 1024)

  reply = control.exchange("display-message -p alive", timeout: 0.5)
  Example.check(reply.blocks.last.body == "alive\n", "slow reader blocked commands")
  Example.check(reply.attribution == :boundary_window, "reply overclaims attribution")
  Example.check(reliable.diagnostics.fetch(:overflowed), "overflow is missing from diagnostics")
  Example.check(control.diagnostics.fetch(:retained_reply_bytes).zero?, "consumed reply remains retained")
  reliable.next(timeout: 0.5)
  Example.raises(LibTmux::SubscriptionOverflow) { reliable.next(timeout: 0.5) }
  gap = tail.next(timeout: 0.5)
  Example.check(gap.kind == :gap && gap.dropped_bytes.positive?, "tail hid lost bytes")
end
```

# libtmux Drive tmux from Ruby: [sessions][session], [windows][window] and [panes][pane] as handles, [snapshots][snapshot] you filter in plain Ruby, and [control connections][controlconnection] that report what tmux does. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) [![compatibility](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml) [![libtmux](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux?label=libtmux)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/LICENSE)
Part of [libtmux for Ruby](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby#readme). This gem is the core; the [packages below](#packages) build on it. [Create][server-new_session] and [split][pane-split] windows, [read][server-snapshot] and [filter][selection-where] what a server holds, and [type into a pane][pane-send_text] and capture what it shows. It suits scripts, tests that need a real tmux, and tools that drive a terminal program. [Cancel][cancellation-cancel] a request that is waiting, and [follow events][controlconnection-subscribe] as tmux emits them. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Find things](#find-sessions-windows-and-panes) · [Create](#create-sessions-windows-and-panes) · [Type and read](#type-into-a-pane-and-read-it-back) · [Your own server](#use-the-tmux-server-you-already-run) · [Cancel](#wait-time-out-and-cancel) · [Link windows](#link-a-window-into-several-sessions) · [Options](#read-and-set-options-and-hooks) · [Watch tmux](#watch-tmux-change) · [Groups](#run-several-commands-in-order) · [Packages](#packages) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the gem. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer on `PATH`: ```console $ gem install libtmux ``` This program creates a session, adds a window, splits it, and prints each window with its panes: ```ruby require "libtmux" snapshot = LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session( name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"] ) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.snapshot end snapshot.windows.each do |window| puts "#{window.name}: #{window.panes.map(&:id).join(', ')}" end ``` Save it as `quickstart.rb` and run it: ```console $ ruby quickstart.rb ``` It prints: ```text main: %0 logs: %1, %2 ``` [`Server.start`][server-start] gives the program a tmux server of its own, on its own socket with an empty configuration, and closes it when the block exits. It never touches a tmux you already use. Requiring the gem starts no tmux process. ## Find sessions, windows, and panes ### [`Server#list_sessions`][server-list_sessions]: what tmux has now One call asks tmux for every session and returns frozen handles in numeric ID order. [`list_windows`][server-list_windows] and [`list_panes`][server-list_panes] are its siblings, and [`Session#list_windows`][session-list_windows] and [`Window#list_panes`][window-list_panes] narrow them: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) sessions = server.list_sessions puts "sessions: #{sessions.map(&:id).sort.join(', ')}" end ``` It runs on a private server and prints: ```text sessions: $0, $1 ``` An empty array means tmux answered with nothing to list. A listing that fails raises [`CommandError`][commanderror]. ### [`Server#snapshot`][server-snapshot]: one read, many queries Read the server once, then filter that read with [`where`][selection-where], [`select`][selection-select], [`one`][selection-one] and [`one_or_nil`][selection-one_or_nil]. These queries make no tmux calls: ```ruby require "libtmux" snapshot = LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session( name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"] ) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.snapshot end panes = snapshot.panes active_ids = panes.where(active: true).map(&:id) wide_panes = panes.select { |pane| pane.width >= 40 } panes_by_window = panes.group_by { |pane| pane.window.name } logs = snapshot.windows.one(name: "logs") missing = snapshot.windows.one_or_nil(name: "missing") puts "active: #{active_ids.join(', ')}" puts "wide: #{wide_panes.map(&:id).join(', ')}" puts "logs panes: #{logs.panes.length}" puts "missing: #{missing.inspect}" ``` It prints: ```text active: %0, %1 wide: %0, %1 logs panes: 2 missing: nil ``` `one` raises [`NoMatchError`][nomatcherror] or [`MultipleMatchesError`][multiplematcheserror] unless exactly one record matches. `one_or_nil` returns `nil` for no match and still rejects duplicates. A selection keeps the membership it captured, so call `server.snapshot` again to read later changes. The [field catalog](../../docs/reference/fields.md) lists every query field and wire name. ### [`Server#search_panes`][server-search_panes]: the matching panes in one call `search_panes` captures the server and answers a selection of the panes whose fields match `where:`. This program also uses the snapshot queries above: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| work = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"], receipt: true) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) snapshot = server.snapshot session = snapshot.sessions.where(name: "work").one puts "matching session: #{session.name}" missing = snapshot.sessions.one_or_nil(name: "missing") puts "missing session: #{missing.nil?}" panes = server.search_panes(where: {id: work.pane.id}) puts "matching pane: #{panes.one.id}" end ``` It prints: ```text matching session: work missing session: true matching pane: %0 ``` ### [`Server#explain_panes`][server-explain_panes]: what runs in tmux, what runs in Ruby `explain_panes` returns the plan for a pane query and sends nothing to tmux. Today tmux returns the whole server and Ruby applies every criterion: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) criteria = {active: true} plan = server.explain_panes(where: criteria) puts "tmux reads: #{plan.fetch(:capture)}" puts "tmux filters: #{plan.fetch(:pushed) || 'nothing'}" puts "Ruby filters: #{plan.fetch(:residual).fetch('where').keys.join(', ')}" puts "matching panes: #{server.search_panes(where: criteria).length}" end ``` It prints: ```text tmux reads: full_graph tmux filters: nothing Ruby filters: active matching panes: 1 ``` ## Create sessions, windows, and panes ### [`Server#new_session`][server-new_session]: a session and its first window `new_session` starts a detached session that runs `command:`, an argv array. Ask for a receipt to read the IDs tmux assigned to the session, window and pane: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| created = server.new_session( name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"], receipt: true ) puts "session: #{created.entity.id}" puts "window: #{created.window.id}" puts "pane: #{created.pane.id}" end ``` It prints: ```text session: $0 window: @0 pane: %0 ``` Creation returns once tmux has assigned the IDs. It says nothing about whether the program started or exited cleanly. ### [`Session#new_window`][session-new_window]: add a window [`Pane#split`][pane-split] and [`Window#split`][window-split] add panes the same way. A new window takes a `name:` and the same `command:` as a session: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) puts "window: #{window.snapshot.name}" puts "session windows: #{session.list_windows.length}" end ``` It prints: ```text window: logs session windows: 2 ``` - `cwd:` names a directory on the machine running Ruby, and is checked before the command is sent. - `environment:` is a String-to-String map of literal values. - `new_window(index:)` refuses a slot that is taken. - [`Pane#split`][pane-split] targets that exact pane, and `size:` is a cell count or a percentage string such as `"40%"`. - New windows and splits keep focus unless you pass `focus: true`. The full contract is in [Creation][behavior-creation]. ## Type into a pane and read it back ### [`Pane#send_text`][pane-send_text]: type, then read what the pane showed `send_text` types literal text, and [`send_keys`][pane-send_keys] sends tmux key names such as `Enter`. [`Pane#capture`][pane-capture] reads the screen. To wait for output, poll the pane until the line appears. A [control connection][server-open_control] reports it as an event instead, but needs tmux 3.7 or newer: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| created = server.new_session( name: "capture", command: ["/bin/sh"], environment: {"ENV" => "/dev/null"}, receipt: true ) pane = created.pane pane.send_text("printf '\\nlibtmux capture ready\\n'") pane.send_keys("Enter") deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + 5 captured = pane.capture.stdout.lines(chomp: true) until captured.include?("libtmux capture ready") raise "Output did not arrive within five seconds" if Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline sleep 0.05 captured = pane.capture.stdout.lines(chomp: true) end raise "Expected output is absent from the pane" unless captured.include?("libtmux capture ready") puts "libtmux capture ready" end ``` It prints: ```text libtmux capture ready ``` - Sending input does not show that the shell finished the command. - `capture` returns the visible screen. `start:` and `finish:` choose a range, and `join:` joins wrapped lines. - `escapes:`, `escape_bytes:`, `preserve_trailing:` and `trim_trailing:` change the bytes it returns. - `mode_screen:`, `alternate:` and `pending:` read a copy-mode screen, the saved screen and an unfinished escape sequence. Pass at most one. - Binary buffers keep their trailing newlines. See [`write_buffer`][server-write_buffer] and [`read_buffer`][server-read_buffer] in the [layout and bytes recipe](../../docs/recipes.md#layout-and-bytes). The full contract is in [Pane input and capture][behavior-capture]. ## Use the tmux server you already run ### [`Server.new`][server-new]: borrow a daemon [`Server.open`][server-open] and [`Server.new`][server-new] bind an endpoint that already exists. Closing the binding retires its clients and leaves the daemon running; [`Server#kill`][server-kill] stops it. The outer [`Server.start`][server-start] block here only supplies a daemon to borrow: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |owner| owner.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server = LibTmux::Server.new(endpoint: owner.endpoint) begin puts "connected sessions: #{server.list_sessions.length}" ensure server.close end puts "sessions after client close: #{owner.list_sessions.length}" end ``` It prints: ```text connected sessions: 1 sessions after client close: 1 ``` - [`Endpoint.new`][endpoint-new] takes a socket path or socket name. With neither, it picks the socket tmux would: `LIBTMUX_SOCKET_PATH`, `LIBTMUX_SOCKET`, the server `$TMUX` names, then tmux's default socket. [`Endpoint.from_env`][endpoint-from_env] follows `$TMUX` alone. - A binding keeps a private link to the socket it bound, so commands never reach a different daemon that later takes the same path. - A ref is valid on the server that issued it. Another server raises [`TargetNotFoundError`][targetnotfounderror]. See [ownership and errors](../../docs/ownership-errors.md). ## Wait, time out, and cancel ### [`Cancellation.new`][cancellation-new]: wake a request that is waiting Typed operations take `timeout:` and `cancel:`. Pass a [`Cancellation`][cancellation] token as `cancel:`, call [`cancel`][cancellation-cancel] from another thread to wake the request, join its callers, then [`close`][cancellation-close] the token: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) cancellation = LibTmux::Cancellation.new waiting = Thread.new do server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"], timeout: 5, cancel: cancellation) rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error error end server.wait_for("ready", timeout: 5) cancellation.cancel failure = waiting.value puts "request: #{failure.class}" puts "delivery: #{failure.delivery}" cancellation.close end ``` It prints: ```text request: LibTmux::Cancelled delivery: possibly_sent ``` [`Cancelled`][cancelled] reports `delivery` as `:not_sent` or `:possibly_sent`. Cancelling does not undo what tmux already queued. The [plain-Ruby recipe](../../examples/cancel.rb) also checks that the client was reaped. The contracts are in [Cancellation tokens][behavior-cancellation] and [ownership and errors](../../docs/ownership-errors.md). ## Link a window into several sessions ### [`Session#link_window`][session-link_window]: one window at several indexes A [`WindowLink`][windowlink] keeps a session, an index and a window ID together, so a window linked twice stays one window. `link_window` needs an explicit `index:`: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "links", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) session.link_window(window.ref, index: 4) session.link_window(window.ref, index: 9) links = session.list_window_links puts "indexes: #{links.map(&:index).join(', ')}" puts "windows: #{links.map { |link| link.window.id }.uniq.join(', ')}" end ``` It prints: ```text indexes: 0, 4, 9 windows: @0 ``` - Select, unlink, move, swap and display check the whole link identity in the same tmux queue turn as the operation, so a stale link never becomes its replacement. - Rewriting command aliases during an operation is outside that guarantee. The contract is in [Window links][behavior-window-links], and the [linked-windows recipe](../../docs/recipes.md#one-window-at-three-indexes) runs this at three indexes. ## Read and set options and hooks ### [`Session#options`][session-options]: a value with its inheritance [`Options#set`][options-set] writes an option at the scope of its accessor. [`Options#get`][options-get] reads it back as an [`OptionValue`][optionvalue], and [`as`][optionvalue-as] converts it strictly. [`Hooks#set`][hooks-set] stores a tmux command: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) session.options.set("history-limit", 5000) limit = session.options.get("history-limit") puts "history-limit: #{limit.as(:integer)}" puts "inherited: #{limit.inherited?}" session.hooks.set("after-new-window", command: "display-message created") puts "hook: #{session.hooks.get('after-new-window').as(:string)}" end ``` It prints: ```text history-limit: 5000 inherited: false hook: display-message created ``` - An [`OptionValue`][optionvalue] keeps the raw bytes, whether the value is inherited, and the array index. `as` takes `:bytes`, `:string`, `:integer` or `:boolean`. - A missing array index raises [`NoMatchError`][nomatcherror], and a present empty value stays present. - Reading an array without an index raises [`MultipleMatchesError`][multiplematcheserror] when it has several entries. - Hook values stay tmux command strings, and indexed hooks run in index order. The contracts are in [Options and hooks][behavior-options] and [Option values][behavior-option-values]. ## Watch tmux change ### [`Server#open_control`][server-open_control]: events as they happen A [`ControlConnection`][controlconnection] runs a command with [`exchange`][controlconnection-exchange] and streams what tmux reports through [`subscribe`][controlconnection-subscribe]. The subscription's [`next`][controlsubscription-next] waits for the next [`ControlEvent`][controlevent]: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) server.open_control(session: session.ref) do |control| reply = control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 5) puts "reply: #{reply.blocks.last.body.strip}" events = control.subscribe(max_events: 64, max_bytes: 65_536) window.rename("renamed") event = nil until event&.raw&.start_with?("%window-renamed") event = events.next(timeout: 5) end puts "event: #{event.raw.strip}" end end ``` It prints: ```text reply: ready event: %window-renamed @0 renamed ``` - `exchange` answers a [`GuardedReply`][guardedreply]. It holds the blocks seen between two boundaries, and a hook can print into the same interval. - A subscription is bounded. A reliable one raises [`SubscriptionOverflow`][subscriptionoverflow] when it falls behind, and a tail one reports the lost range as a `:gap` event. - [`pause_output`][controlconnection-pause_output] and [`resume_output`][controlconnection-resume_output] return a [`GuardedReply`][guardedreply]. A reply does not show that the action took effect. - To reconnect, close the old connection and pass it as `open_control(session: ref, reconnect: old_connection)`. The replacement has a new `generation`, and every new subscription starts with a `:reconnect` gap. Nothing is replayed. The contracts are in [Control connections][behavior-control], and the [control overflow recipe](../../docs/recipes.md#control-overflow) runs both subscription modes. ## Run several commands in order ### [`Server#run_group`][server-run_group]: several commands through one client A group submits several tmux commands in order through one client. The [`GroupResult`][groupresult] holds one aggregate status, and each step reports `unknown`: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) group = server.run_group([ ["set-option", "-g", "@before", "kept"], ["select-pane", "-t", "%4294967294"], ["set-option", "-g", "@after", "never run"] ]) puts "success: #{group.success?}" puts "steps: #{group.steps.map { |step| step.fetch(:outcome) }.join(', ')}" puts "@before: #{server.options(scope: :session).get('@before').as(:string)}" end ``` It prints: ```text success: false steps: unknown, unknown, unknown @before: kept ``` The first command keeps its effect when the second fails, and the third never runs. The [group recipe](../../docs/recipes.md#failure-inside-a-group) checks the same. ## Packages Start with `libtmux`. Add the companion for your caller: | Gem | Require | Use it for | | --- | --- | --- | | [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux) | `libtmux` | Blocking scripts, snapshots, and control connections | | [libtmux-async](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-async) | `libtmux/async` | Concurrent commands and bounded streams in Async tasks | | [libtmux-mcp](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-mcp) | `libtmux/mcp` | An MCP server with explicit endpoints and tool policy | | [libtmux-workspace](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-workspace) | `libtmux/workspace` | YAML/JSON workspace plans and a CLI to apply them | ### [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux): the core This gem: blocking [server][server], [session][session], [window][window] and [pane][pane] handles, immutable [snapshots][snapshot], and [control connections][controlconnection]. The sections above run against it. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) ### [libtmux-async](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-async): concurrent commands Concurrent commands and bounded control streams inside an Async task that your application owns. Require `libtmux/async`, then open a scope with [`LibTmux::Async.open`][async-open]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/libtmux-async/) · [Guide](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/async/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-async) ```console $ gem install libtmux-async ``` Capture every pane concurrently with [`Scope#map`][async-scope-map]: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| refs = scope.server.list_panes.map(&:ref) screens = scope.map(refs, concurrency: 2) do |ref| scope.server.pane(ref).capture end puts "captured panes: #{screens.length}" puts "all succeeded: #{screens.all?(&:success?)}" end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text captured panes: 2 all succeeded: true ``` ### [libtmux-mcp](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-mcp): a tmux server for MCP clients An MCP server over stdio for one tmux server, with an explicit tool policy. Installs `libtmux-mcp`; require `libtmux/mcp` to embed it through [`LibTmux::MCP::Application`][mcp-application]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/reference/) · [Tools](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) ```console $ gem install libtmux-mcp ``` Add the server to Claude Code. `--start-session work` starts a tmux server on the socket `agent` when none answers there, with a session named `work`, and stops it when the server exits. Until you enable more tools, the server serves [`tmux_capabilities`][tool-tmux_capabilities] and [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: ```console $ claude mcp add tmux -- libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --start-session work \ --endpoint dev ``` The [MCP README](../libtmux-mcp/README.md) covers other clients, every tool and authored shell commands. ### [libtmux-workspace](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-workspace): YAML workspaces YAML or JSON workspaces, validated, planned offline and applied to an open server. Installs `libtmux-workspace`; require `libtmux/workspace` to use it from Ruby through [`LibTmux::Workspace`][workspace]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/reference/) · [Command reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/cli/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-workspace) ```console $ gem install libtmux-workspace ``` Save this workspace as `workspace.yaml`: ```yaml session_name: work environment: PROJECT_MODE: development windows: - window_name: editor window_index: 1 layout: tiled panes: - shell_command: printf 'editor ready\n' - {} ``` Check it without contacting tmux: ```console $ libtmux-workspace validate workspace.yaml ``` ```text Workspace configuration is valid. ``` The [workspace README](../libtmux-workspace/README.md) loads it into a running server and lists every option. ## What it leaves out - **Live objects.** A [snapshot record][snapshot] is what tmux said when you read it, and a [handle][server-list_sessions] reads tmux again each time you list. See [Captured records][behavior-records] and [Live handles][behavior-live-handles]. - **A terminal emulator.** [`Pane#capture`][pane-capture] returns the bytes tmux holds for the screen, with the flags above to shape them. - **A server it starts unasked.** [`Server.new`][server-new] and [`Server.open`][server-open] bind a running server; only [`Server.start`][server-start] starts one. With no socket named, [`Endpoint.new`][endpoint-new] picks the socket tmux would, so a program run inside tmux reaches that tmux. - **Replay.** A reconnected control connection reports a gap and never replays requests or missed output. See [Control flow][behavior-control-flow]. - **Transactions.** A [group][server-run_group] runs in order and keeps the effects of the steps before a failure. - **Whole-program typing.** RBS declarations ship with the gem. See [Signature proof][behavior-signature]. ## Support and status - **Unstable API.** Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and any release may change or remove exported identifiers. Pin an exact version. Imports start no scheduler, tmux server or background task. A scope borrows a core [`Server`][server] and leaves its daemon running when the scope exits. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Cancel](#cancel-a-request-without-stalling-the-others) · [Map](#keep-results-ordered-and-bounded) · [Control](#read-control-events-in-a-scope) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the gem. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer on `PATH`: ```console $ gem install libtmux-async ``` Open a scope over a core server with [`LibTmux::Async.open`][async-open], then capture every pane concurrently with [`Scope#map`][async-scope-map]. The outer [`Server.start`][server-start] block only supplies a server for the scope to borrow: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| refs = scope.server.list_panes.map(&:ref) screens = scope.map(refs, concurrency: 2) do |ref| scope.server.pane(ref).capture end puts "captured panes: #{screens.length}" puts "all succeeded: #{screens.all?(&:success?)}" end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text captured panes: 2 all succeeded: true ``` - Leave out `parent:` to use the current Async task. - A scope rejects use from another thread, process or scheduler, so create one scope for each scheduler thread. - Scope exit retires its clients and joins its owned tasks. ## Cancel a request without stalling the others ### [`Async::Server#run`][async-server-run]: cancel a request that is waiting `scope.server.run` waits for a tmux command in a task. Cancel that task and the scope retires its client, while sibling requests keep running. [`wait_for`][async-server-wait_for] returns once the request has signalled that it is running, so the cancel arrives while it waits: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| waiting = parent.async do scope.server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"], timeout: 5) rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error error end scope.server.wait_for("ready", timeout: 5) waiting.cancel failure = waiting.wait puts "request: #{failure.class}" puts "delivery: #{failure.delivery}" end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text request: LibTmux::Cancelled delivery: possibly_sent ``` - `run` returns the same binary [`CommandResult`][commandresult] as the core. - [`Cancelled`][cancelled] carries `delivery` as `:not_sent` or `:possibly_sent`. A deadline cannot undo tmux effects. - Interactive terminal attachment stays on the blocking core and raises [`UnsupportedFeatureError`][unsupportedfeatureerror] here. The [complete program](../../examples/async_cancel.rb) also keeps capturing while the request waits, and checks that the cancelled client is reaped. The contract is in [Async scope][behavior-async-scope]. ## Keep results ordered and bounded ### [`Scope#map`][async-scope-map]: input order, capped payloads `map` runs a block for each item, up to `concurrency:` at a time, and returns a frozen Array in input order. The quick start is a `map`. These limits apply to every scope: | Scope limit | Default | | --- | --- | | Active subprocess clients | 4 | | Admitted subprocess requests, including unconsumed results | 32 | | Queued request payload | 4 MiB | | Retained process and map output payload | 8 MiB | | Per-command stdout / stderr | 1 MiB / 256 KiB | | Control connections | 4 | | Ordinary command deadline | 5 seconds | - Independent requests may complete out of order, and the result is still in input order. - `map` caps retained items and counts payload bytes of strings, primitive values, [`CommandResult`][commandresult], Arrays and Hashes. Cycles and deep nesting are refused. - An application-defined result needs a `result_bytes:` callable that returns a nonnegative Integer. - Keep measured values unchanged until the map returns. The counts cover payload bytes and do not measure the Ruby heap. The contract is in [Async map][behavior-async-map]. ## Read control events in a scope ### [`Async::Server#open_control`][async-server-open_control]: replies and events A control connection has its own request, reply and subscriber limits. [`exchange`][async-controlconnection-exchange] runs one command, and [`events`][async-controlconnection-events] yields what tmux reports outside a reply: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| scope.server.open_control(session: session.ref) do |control| reply = control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 5) puts "reply: #{reply.blocks.last.body.strip}" events = control.events window.rename("renamed") event = events.next(timeout: 5) until event&.raw&.start_with?("%window-renamed") puts "event: #{event.raw.strip}" end end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text reply: ready event: %window-renamed @0 renamed ``` - `exchange` answers a [`GuardedReply`][guardedreply] with `:boundary_window` attribution. It makes no claim that the command finished. - Events arrive through `events.next` or an explicit [`subscribe`][async-controlconnection-subscribe]. Consumer callbacks run outside the parser. - A reliable subscription raises on overflow, and a tail subscription reports the dropped range. - Cancelling a dispatched exchange that is not drained closes the connection. - [`pause_output`][async-controlconnection-pause_output] and [`resume_output`][async-controlconnection-resume_output] report possible loss through gap events. A gap does not show that the action took effect. - To reconnect, close the connection and pass it as `reconnect:`. The replacement stays owned by the scope, has a new generation, and starts with a gap of unknown loss. Nothing is replayed. The contract is in [Control connections][behavior-control]. ## What it leaves out - **Terminal attachment.** `attach` stays on the blocking core and raises [`UnsupportedFeatureError`][unsupportedfeatureerror] on this facade. - **Replay.** Reconnect and resume never replay requests or missed output. See [Control connections][behavior-control]. - **A scheduler.** Imports start no scheduler or background task, and your application owns the Async root task. See [Execution modes][doc-modes]. - **Cross-thread scopes.** A scope belongs to the thread, process and scheduler that opened it. See [Async scope][behavior-async-scope]. ## Support and status - **Unstable API.** Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and any release may change or remove exported identifiers. Pin an exact version. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and the [main changelog](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for changes that span gems. - **Ruby 3.3 or newer** and **tmux 3.3a or newer.** The facade runs through a core server, so it refuses an older daemon the same way. - **Control connections need tmux 3.7 or newer.** [`open_control`][async-server-open_control] refuses an older daemon before a control client attaches. - **Dependencies.** The gem needs `async` and `libtmux` at the same version as itself; the gemspec pins the range. - **Linux, including WSL, and macOS.** CI runs on Linux; macOS is best effort. See the [compatibility workflow][compat] and the [CI matrix](../../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#running-ci-against-any-tmux). ## Documentation | | | | --- | --- | | # libtmux-mcp Expose a tmux server over MCP stdio. Read snapshots, capture pane output and wait for events, or enable creation, input and shell commands one tool at a time. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/reference/) · [Tools](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) [![compatibility](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml) [![libtmux-mcp](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-mcp?label=libtmux-mcp)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/LICENSE)
Part of [libtmux for Ruby](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby#readme). Built on [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux) and [libtmux-async](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-async). An MCP client starts `libtmux-mcp` and talks to it over stdin and stdout. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Connect a client](#connect-a-client) · [Choose the server](#choose-which-tmux-server-it-serves) · [The tools](#the-tools) · [Read](#read-the-layout-and-the-screen) · [Create](#create-type-and-close) · [Run](#run-a-script-in-a-pane) · [Embed](#embed-it-in-ruby) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the gem and its `libtmux-mcp` executable. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer: ```console $ gem install libtmux-mcp ``` Add the server to Claude Code. `--start-session work` starts a tmux server on the socket `agent` when none answers there, with a session named `work`, and stops it when the server exits. Until you enable more tools, the server serves [`tmux_capabilities`][tool-tmux_capabilities] and [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: ```console $ claude mcp add tmux -- libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --start-session work \ --endpoint dev ``` Run by hand, `libtmux-mcp` waits for input until EOF. `libtmux-mcp --help` lists every option. ## Connect a client ### `claude mcp add`: Claude Code The command in the quick start registers the server with Claude Code. ### `codex mcp add`: Codex CLI Codex CLI takes the same command after `--`: ```console $ codex mcp add tmux -- libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --start-session work \ --endpoint dev ``` ### `mcpServers`: clients that read JSON A client that reads a JSON configuration, such as Claude Desktop's `claude_desktop_config.json`, takes the same command as an `mcpServers` entry: ```json { "mcpServers": { "tmux": { "command": "libtmux-mcp", "args": ["--socket-name", "agent", "--start-session", "work", "--endpoint", "dev"] } } } ``` If the client does not start servers with your shell's `PATH`, set `command` to the absolute path that `command -v libtmux-mcp` prints. ## Choose which tmux server it serves ### `--socket` and `--socket-name`: pick the daemon Set `TMUX_SOCKET` to an existing tmux socket. This command borrows that daemon and serves MCP on stdin and stdout: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket "$TMUX_SOCKET" \ --endpoint local ``` Use `--socket-name NAME` instead of `--socket PATH` to select a named socket, as the quick start does. - With neither flag, the server borrows the socket in `LIBTMUX_SOCKET_PATH`, else the name in `LIBTMUX_SOCKET`, else the server `TMUX` names when it runs inside tmux, else tmux's default socket. When both variables are set, the path wins, and an empty variable counts as unset. A flag ignores both variables, and the two flags are refused together. - Without `--start-session`, the server never starts a tmux server. When none answers at the socket it chose, it exits with status 1. - Started from a tmux pane with no flag or variable, the server drives that pane's server. Pass `--socket-name` to give an agent a server of its own. - EOF retires the clients the server owns and leaves a borrowed daemon running. - `--endpoint` sets the public alias in discovery and resource URIs, and defaults to `local`. ### `--start-session`: start the server too `--start-session NAME` starts a tmux server on the socket the other flags choose when none answers there. The server has an empty configuration and one session named `NAME`, which runs your default shell: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --start-session work ``` - A server that already answers is borrowed as it is. The flag creates no session in it and stops nothing. - EOF stops the server the flag started. Add `--keep` to leave it running, for example to attach to it from a terminal. - A fresh server's first pane is `%0`. - `NAME` starts with a letter or digit, then takes letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 128 characters. ## The tools Each tool name links to its page on libtmux.org, with the arguments, limits and result schema. Repeat `--enable-tool` for each additional tool. | Tools | Default | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | [`tmux_capabilities`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_capabilities/), [`tmux_snapshot`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_snapshot/) | Enabled | Discover capabilities and query captured metadata | | [`tmux_capture`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_capture/), [`tmux_wait`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_wait/) | Disabled | Capture a screen or wait for text/process exit | | [`tmux_create`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_create/), [`tmux_send`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_send/), [`tmux_close`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_close/) | Disabled | Create entities, send text/keys and tear down exact targets | | [`tmux_run`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_run/) | Disabled | Run a script in an explicitly enrolled zsh shell | - Disabled tools are absent from discovery and denied on direct application calls. - An unknown tool name is refused when the server starts. The [complete protocol recipe](../../examples/mcp_protocol.rb) exercises discovery, snapshots, default denial, enabled mutations, cancellation and EOF cleanup through actual pipes, including the installed executable. ## Read the layout and the screen ### [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: the layout, in pages - Pages come from one immutable capture, and a cursor continues that capture. - An expired, evicted or foreign cursor returns an error. The server never substitutes a fresh listing. ### [`tmux_capture`][tool-tmux_capture]: a pane's screen Enable the screen tools together: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket "$TMUX_SOCKET" \ --enable-tool tmux_capture \ --enable-tool tmux_wait ``` - It reads a bounded screen and keeps its line endings. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 come back base64-encoded. - With tracking, a call returns a cursor, and later calls return a splice against that exact captured state. A cursor from another server generation or from a respawned pane is refused. - It refuses a pane whose effective `after-capture-pane` hook is not empty, including inherited entries. - On tmux 3.3a to 3.4 the hook is checked before the capture command runs, so keep hook configuration stable while observing. ### [`tmux_wait`][tool-tmux_wait]: wait for text or exit - It waits for screen text, or for the pane process to exit. Screen text comes from control events on tmux 3.7 and newer, and from polling on older daemons, which take no control client. - Wrapped rows are joined, so text that the pane width split across rows still matches. - If the pane, or the tmux server holding it, ends before the text appears, the call fails with `pane_died`, `delivery: observed` and the last rows it read in the error's `capture`. If only the control stream ends while the pane lives, such as after the client detaches, the failure is `observation_lost`. - A cancelled or expired wait closes its observers and never signals the pane program. - Process tracking needs native process identity. Without it, the call is refused. ### [Resource templates][mcp-resources]: the same data as URIs [`tmux_metadata`][resource-tmux_metadata], [`tmux_metadata_page`][resource-tmux_metadata_page] and [`tmux_screen`][resource-tmux_screen] expose metadata pages and pane screens under endpoint and generation URIs, with the same policy and limits as their tools. - The server does not advertise resource subscriptions. - [Snapshots, cursors and references][mcp-snapshots-topic] has the full contract. ## Create, type and close ### [`tmux_create`][tool-tmux_create]: new sessions, windows and panes Enable the three tools together: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --start-session work \ --enable-tool tmux_create \ --enable-tool tmux_send \ --enable-tool tmux_close ``` - It takes argument arrays as `argv`. - Results carry the references tmux returned. ### [`tmux_send`][tool-tmux_send]: literal text or named keys - Text and keys are separate variants. - It reports `dispatch_only`: the input was dispatched, and the command has not necessarily finished. - After a cancellation, the effect stays unknown and is not reported as none. ### [`tmux_close`][tool-tmux_close]: an exact target - It takes an exact session, window or pane reference, and never selects by name. ## Run a script in a pane ### [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run]: authored commands in an enrolled zsh [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run] runs a POSIX script in a pane's interactive zsh 5.9. It needs both the tool and an enrolled pane. Enable the tool and write a setup file for one exact pane. The first pane of the server that `--start-session` starts is `%0`; on a server you started another way, read the pane IDs with [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --start-session work \ --enable-tool tmux_run \ --enroll-pane %0=enroll.zsh ``` Then, in that pane's zsh, run `source enroll.zsh`. A relative path resolves from the directory where the server starts. - `--enroll-pane` requires `--enable-tool tmux_run`, and each pane and each file may appear once. - The server writes a private file (mode `0600`) and never types into the terminal. It refuses an existing file or a symlink. - Setup files expire. `--enrollment-timeout SECONDS` sets the lifetime, at most 300. - EOF retires pending enrollment and removes only the files the server wrote. - A call takes an exact pane `target`, a POSIX `script`, and optional `stdout_limit` and `stderr_limit` byte counts. - The script runs with the shell's working directory and exported environment. - Stdout and stderr come back separately, as UTF-8 or base64. - A nonzero exit or a signal is a completion result. Output over its limit is an error with completion unobserved, and never a truncated success. - Cancelling a run does not prove that its child processes stopped. ## Embed it in Ruby Require `libtmux/mcp`. Imports start no tmux process, scheduler or MCP server. The [execution guide](../../docs/modes.md) covers result and ownership boundaries. ### [`LibTmux::MCP::Application`][mcp-application]: serve from your own program [`Application`][mcp-application] borrows an application-owned [`LibTmux::Async::Server`][async-server]. Its [`sdk_server`][mcp-application-sdk_server] supplies the SDK server that [`StdioTransport`][mcp-stdiotransport] consumes: ```ruby application = LibTmux::MCP::Application.new(server: scope.server, endpoint_name: "example") sdk = application.sdk_server input, client_input = IO.pipe client_output, output = IO.pipe transport = LibTmux::MCP::StdioTransport.new(server: sdk, parent: parent, input: input, output: output) runner = parent.async { transport.run } ``` The [complete program](../../examples/mcp_protocol.rb) runs this excerpt inside an Async task with an open [`LibTmux::Async`][async] scope. It sends real JSON-RPC messages through the pipes, checks the replies, and prints `PASS mcp_protocol`. ### [`Application#invite_shell`][mcp-application-invite_shell]: enroll a shell from Ruby Call `invite_shell` with a pane reference, `timeout:` and `expires_in:`, then pass the invitation to [`accept_shell`][mcp-application-accept_shell]. - The invitation's `shell_arguments` make up the setup command to source in that pane's zsh. - `timeout:` bounds acquisition, and `expires_in:` sets the enrollment lifetime. - The application owns invitations and accepted connections until [`close`][mcp-application-close]. Direct enrollment calls enforce tool policy. ## What it leaves out - **Tools you have not enabled.** Disabled tools are absent from discovery, and a direct application call is denied. See [The tools](#the-tools). - **Resource subscriptions.** The server does not advertise them. See the [resource templates][mcp-resources]. - **Typing into your terminal.** The server writes a private setup file and never types into a pane's terminal to enroll it. See [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run]. - **A guaranteed stop.** Cancelling a run does not prove that its child processes stopped. See [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run]. ## Support and status - **Unstable API.** Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and any release may change or remove exported identifiers. Pin an exact version. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and the [main changelog](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for changes that span gems. - **Ruby 3.3 or newer** and **tmux 3.3a or newer.** The server refuses an older daemon when it starts, before it serves any tool, and prints the reason and the remedy on stderr. - **A daemon that changes while it runs.** A tool call returns an `unsupported` result with `delivery: not_sent`. The result names the floor and says to upgrade tmux and restart the server. - **The `screen_contains` wait.** It uses control events on tmux 3.7 and newer and polls the pane screen on older daemons. - **Dependencies.** The gem needs `libtmux` and `libtmux-async` at the same version as itself, and the `mcp` SDK. - **Linux, including WSL, and macOS.** CI runs on Linux; macOS is best effort. # libtmux-workspace [Load][workspace-load] bounded YAML or JSON, inspect an immutable [creation plan][workspace-plan-class], then explicitly [apply][workspace-plan-apply] it to an open libtmux server.
